Products should not belong to Suppliers.

sections.title: This Is a Major Milestone
paragraphs: We've now completed what I would call Phase 1: Core Business Foundation.
Everything we've designed so far is reusable across every future module:
None of those modules will need to reinvent customers, products, documents, assets, or inventory—they'll simply build on this foundation.

paragraphs: I think this is the right place to pause and acknowledge the milestone before moving into transactional modules.

sections.title: One Architectural Improvement Before Sales Orders
paragraphs: While designing Quotation, I noticed another pattern that I think will make KoreVity significantly cleaner.

Rather than giving every transaction its own independent line-item structure (Quotation Line, Sales Order Line, Invoice Line, Purchase Order Line, etc.) with duplicated concepts, we should design a shared Transaction Line architecture.
Each transaction can have its own specialized line entity, but they should all inherit the same conceptual structure:
That gives us consistency across Sales, Purchasing, Manufacturing, and even Service, while still allowing each transaction type to add fields unique to its workflow.
I think this will make both the database model and the application code much more maintainable as KoreVity grows.
